Bhuwan Chandra Suyal ---- appellant
Vs
The Registrar cum OL ---- respondent
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
 
1. Ms. Menka Tripathi, learned counsel for the 
appellant.
2. The appeal is directed against order of 
Official Liquidator rejecting the claim of the 
creditor. The winding up has been ordered in 
Company Petition No. 04 of 2012, and the 
winding up is being monitored by the Court. 
Consequently, the appeal will lie to the same 
Court which is seized of the matter.
3. Office is directed to list the instant appeal 
before the Single Judge who is having roster to 
decide Company Petition No. 04 of 2012.
4. List on 12.03.2026, as fresh.
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)

Kumar Chauhan, Advocates for the

As soon as these matters were taken 
up, learned counsel appearing for the 
petitioners in COMP No.4 of 2012 submits 
that the workmen’s claim is already 
pending in that petition. Therefore, any 
order passed by the Registrar Cum Official 
Liquidator may not be subject to appeal 
with regard to the same claim, which is 
already pending in the COMP No.4 of 2012.
Ms. Divya Tiwari, Advocate holding 
brief of Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, Advocate 
submits that Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, 
Advocate is not present today. She seeks 
time. 
List this matter on 14.05.2026.
 (Ravindra Maithani J.)

Ms. Menka Tripathi, Advocate for the

Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, Advocate for the 
respondent. 
Heard on Delay Condonation 
Application, IA No.1 of 2026. 
Having considered, this Court is of the 
view that there are good grounds to condone 
the delay. Accordingly, the Delay Condonation 
Application deserves to be allowed.
The delay condonation application is 
allowed. 
The delay in preferring the appeal is 
condoned. 
Let the respondent file his response 
within three weeks. 
A week, thereafter, rejoinder affidavit, if 
any, may be filed. 
List thereafter for final hearing. 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.)
